title: What is causal about causal models and representations?
abstract: arXiv:2501.19335v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Causal Bayesian networks are often described as causal because they support reasoning about interventions. Yet interventions are defined in the mathematical model, whereas the resulting model predictions concern the effects of actions in the real world. Consequently, whether and how a causal model makes falsifiable predictions about the effects of actions depends on how actions are interpreted as interventions. This requires specifying which actions correspond to which interventions, a step that is frequently left implicit. We develop a formal framework that separates a causal model from the data-generating process it aims to describe and formalizes interpretations connecting actions to interventions. Within this framework, we prove an impossibility result: no interpretation can simultaneously satisfy a collection of desirable properties while remaining non-circular. translated_title: 因果模型与因果表示中的“因果”究竟指什么？
translated_abstract: 因果贝叶斯网络通常被描述为“因果的”，因为它们支持关于干预的推理。然而，干预是在数学模型中定义的，而模型的预测涉及的是现实世界中行动的效果。因此，因果模型是否以及如何对行动的效果做出可证伪的预测，取决于行动如何被解释为干预。这需要明确哪些行动对应哪些干预，而这一步骤往往被隐式处理。我们开发了一个形式化框架，将因果模型与其旨在描述的数据生成过程分离开来，并将连接行动与干预的解释形式化。在该框架内，我们证明了一个不可能性结果：没有任何解释能够在保持非循环性的同时满足一组期望的性质。在循环解释下，每一个拟合观测数据的模型……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个将因果模型与数据生成过程分离的形式化框架，形式化了连接行动与干预的解释，并证明了不存在能同时满足一组期望性质且保持非循环性的行动-干预解释这一不可能性结果。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a formal framework that separates causal models from the data-generating processes they aim to describe, formalizes interpretations linking actions to interventions, and proves an impossibility result that no interpretation can simultaneously satisfy desirable properties while remaining non-circular.
